Title: Limitations of Current LLM‑Based Software Architecture Design Studies  
Claim: Existing studies on using large language models (LLMs) for software architecture design are limited by isolated case studies and the use of a single LLM, which may not reflect real‑world system design.  
Evidence: "study were isolated from each other, which rarely reflects realworld system design. Investigating how LLMs perform in realistic case studies involving interrelated design decisions, constraints (e.g., team expertise, budget), and tradeoffs is necessary to assess their effectiveness in broader contexts." / "In this study, only one LLM was used to generate design concept alternatives."

Title: Integration of LLMs into Software Architecture Education  
Claim: While LLMs can support students learning software architecture, there is a risk that students may become overly dependent on them, so educators must ensure they are used as learning aids rather than replacements.  
Evidence: "LLMs could help bridge this gap, but the key challenge is ensuring that students use them as learning aids rather than becoming overly dependent on them."
